title: How to Get Free Gym Trials in NZ — Every Major Chain's Trial Policy
meta_desc: Discover how to get free gym trials across NZ's biggest chains, with real prices, contract details, and step‑by‑step claims – no hype, just value.
intro: Nearly 80% of Kiwis test a gym before signing a contract. This guide breaks down every major chain's free trial offer, so you can compare real costs and conditions without the sales fluff.

sections.heading: Why Free Trials Matter
sections.body: A free trial lets you assess equipment, class schedule, and atmosphere without risking a deposit. With most NZ gyms locking you into 12‑month contracts, a trial is the only risk‑free way to confirm the gym fits your lifestyle.

sections.heading: Les Mills – 7‑Day Free Trial
list: Show a NZ driver’s licence or passport
One trial per person, per location
Can be used at any of the 35+ Les Mills clubs nationwide

sections.heading: Anytime Fitness – 3‑Day Free Trial
list: Limited to the specific club you book online
Requires a signed waiver on arrival
ID check (NZ driver’s licence, passport or student card)
Only one active trial per person across the network
Must be booked at least 48 hours in advance

sections.heading: How to Claim Your Free Pass
list: Visit the gym’s official website and locate the “Free Trial” page.
Fill in your name, email, and NZ ID number – no credit‑card required.
Choose your preferred location and date; some chains (Anytime) lock the trial to a single club.
Print the confirmation email or have it on your phone when you arrive.
Sign the waiver, present your ID, and enjoy the facilities within the trial window.
